title: Brown Rice with Cheese and/or Cream Based Sauce, No Added Fat

content.title: About
content.content: Brown rice is a whole‑grain product obtained from unprocessed rice kernels. In this version it is served with a cheese‑ and/or cream‑based sauce, but without any added fat, preserving its nutritional value while keeping the dish light.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Brown rice retains the bran and germ layers, providing more fiber and micronutrients than white rice.
Cheese sauce adds calcium and protein, while cream contributes vitamin D and vitamin A when dairy cream is used.
A dish without added fat is suitable for calorie‑restricted diets yet remains flavorful thanks to the natural fats in cheese and cream.
Brown rice has a lower glycemic index than white rice, helping to maintain stable blood sugar levels.
In some Asian cuisines, rice is traditionally served with a cottage‑cheese‑based sauce, creating a creamy texture without the need for added oil.

items.title: High in Fiber
items.content: The bran layer of brown rice provides soluble and insoluble fiber that supports healthy digestion and satiety.

items.title: Source of Magnesium and Selenium
items.content: Magnesium aids muscle and nerve function, while selenium offers antioxidant protection.

items.title: Calcium from Cheese
items.content: The cheese sauce contributes a substantial amount of calcium, essential for bone and tooth health.

items.title: Combined Plant and Dairy Protein
items.content: Together, rice and cheese deliver a complete amino acid profile useful for tissue repair.

items.title: Low Added Fat Content
items.content: Absence of extra oil reduces overall calories, making the meal suitable for weight‑management plans.

items.title: Lactose Intolerance
items.content: Cheese and cream sauces may cause discomfort for individuals who are lactose intolerant.

items.title: Dairy Allergy
items.content: Some people may experience allergic reactions to cheese or cream.

items.title: Phytic Acid Load
items.content: Brown rice contains phytic acid, which can reduce mineral absorption if consumed in very large amounts.

items.title: Potential High Sodium
items.content: If the sauce is seasoned with salt, monitor intake to avoid excessive sodium consumption.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the rice hot, drizzled with the cheese or cream sauce. Garnish with fresh herbs, spices, or vegetables for extra flavor. It works well as a side dish to meat or fish, or as a light main course on its own.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep dry brown rice in an airtight container in a cool, dry place. Cooked rice with sauce should be refrigerated and consumed within 2‑3 days, reheating to at least 75 °C before serving.
